books.section: Great Depression and the New Deal (1929-1939)

stimulus.text:
Unemployment in the United States, 1929-1941 (percent of the labor force). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics historical series (Economic Report of the President, Table B-22).

| Year | Unemployment rate |
| 1929 | 3.2 percent |
| 1930 | 8.7 percent |
| 1931 | 15.9 percent |
| 1932 | 23.6 percent |
| 1933 | 24.9 percent |
| 1934 | 21.7 percent |
| 1935 | 20.1 percent |
| 1936 | 16.9 percent |
| 1937 | 14.3 percent |
| 1938 | 19.0 percent |
| 1939 | 17.2 percent |
| 1940 | 14.6 percent |
| 1941 | 9.9 percent |
stimulus.source_note: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics historical unemployment series (Economic Report of the President, Table B-22). The books give the same landmarks: about 25 percent in 1933 and 20 percent in 1935.

source: original; table from U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics historical unemployment series
stem: According to the table, how did unemployment change between 1929 and 1933?

options.text: It rose from about 3 percent to about 25 percent
It fell from about 25 percent to about 3 percent
options.misconception: The table runs the other way: about 3 percent in 1929 and about 25 percent in 1933.

options.text: It stayed near 3 percent through the whole period
options.misconception: The table shows unemployment climbing every year from 1929 to 1933, not staying flat.

options.text: It rose to about 25 percent, then fell below 3 percent
options.misconception: Unemployment peaked at about 25 percent in 1933 itself; it had not fallen back by that year.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the table gives 3.2 percent in 1929 and 24.9 percent in 1933, the peak of the Depression.
rationales.B: Background from the books: the direction is reversed: unemployment rose from 1929 to 1933, it did not fall.
rationales.C: Background from the books: the table climbs from 3.2 to 8.9 to 15.9 to 23.6 to 24.9 percent, so it never stayed flat.
rationales.D: Background from the books: 1933 is the peak year in the table at 24.9 percent, not a year of recovery.
rationales.general:
1. Read the 1929 row: unemployment stood at 3.2 percent.
2. Read the 1933 row: it stood at 24.9 percent.
3. That is a rise of roughly eight times in only four years.
4. The table shows the Depression deepening, not easing, up to 1933.
Remember: read a table row by row and compare the two years the question names.
